clay mineral distribution in the Givetian limestones from the Glageon region (Ardenne, France) reflects the sequence stratigraphic and palaeogeographical evolution of the continental margin of a passive margin.
clay and other sediment components are good indicators of the palaeogeographic evolution of the Givet (middle Devonian) continental margin of the Rheic Ocean.

the clay mineral distribution in the middle Devonic limestones of the Ardenne is controlled by regional palaeogeography and sea-level fluctuations and is indicative of warm and variably arid climate, northern and relative to southern terrigenous sources, open sea and restricted environments, tectonic rejuvenations and chemical diagenetic conditions.

the diagenetic and palynostratigraphic significance of clay and other sediment components in the middle Givetian limestones cropping out in the Arde-nne massif, France.
the palaeogeographic and palaeoclimatic implications of clay diagenesis and the diagenetic and palynological implications of the Givetain palaeoclimate.

clay and other sediment components are a key to understanding the sedimentological and palaeogeographical evolution of a passive margin, as well as the diagenetic evolution of its carbonate cover.
the clay mineral assemblage distribution is a good tool for reconstructing palaeogeography and palaeoenvironments, and that the clay diagenesis was controlled by carbonate diagenesis.

the clay mineral distribution in this Givetian succession is controlled by both regional and local factors, the former including palaeogeographic, palaeoclimatic and tectonic conditions, and the latter including palaeomorphological, palaeobathimetric and diagenetic constraints.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the clay mineral distribution is a useful tool for the palaeogeographic reconstruction of ancient carbonate platforms, provided the sedimentary and diagenetic constraints are taken into account.
the clay mineralogy is a useful and complementary tool to the study of the sedimentology and diagenesis of carbonate rocks.
clay mineral assemblage distribution is a powerful tool for reconstructing palaeogeographic and diagenetic evolution of sedimentary rocks.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the clay mineral distribution can provide a reliable palaeogeographical and palaeoenvironmental framework in the absence of other palaeontological data.

, in addition to the well-known diagenetic effects of the carbonate matrix on clay minerals, clay mineral assemblages provide information on the depositional environment and the palaeogeography of carbonate platforms.

, in the absence of major tectonic and/or metamorphic overprint, clay and carbonate mineralogy and petrography can provide a wealth of data on the sedimentary history and the palaeogeographic evolution of the studied area.
